has_subtypes.description: Classic adult-onset HFE-related hemochromatosis caused most often by HFE p.Cys282Tyr homozygosity, with biochemical, clinical, and non-penetrant phenotypes.

evidence.explanation: GeneReviews defines HFE-related hemochromatosis as the HFE homozygous type 1 subtype.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of HFE HC is established in most persons with characteristic laboratory and/or clinical features by identification of HFE p.Cys282Tyr homozygosity.

has_subtypes.name: Type 1

has_subtypes.description: Juvenile-onset autosomal recessive hemochromatosis caused by biallelic HJV pathogenic variants, typically presenting before age 30 with severe iron overload and prominent cardiac and endocrine disease.

evidence.explanation: Case report and literature review distinguishes HJV-related type 2A from HAMP-related type 2B.
evidence.reference_title: Juvenile Hemochromatosis due to a Homozygous Variant in the HJV Gene.
evidence.snippet: Juvenile hemochromatosis type 2a and 2b is an autosomal recessive disease caused by pathogenic variants in HJV and HAMP genes, respectively.

has_subtypes.name: Type 2A

has_subtypes.description: Juvenile-onset autosomal recessive hemochromatosis caused by biallelic HAMP pathogenic variants, producing profound hepcidin deficiency and early severe iron overload.

evidence.explanation: Case report and literature review distinguishes HAMP-related type 2B from HJV-related type 2A.
evidence.reference_title: Juvenile Hemochromatosis due to a Homozygous Variant in the HJV Gene.
evidence.snippet: Juvenile hemochromatosis type 2a and 2b is an autosomal recessive disease caused by pathogenic variants in HJV and HAMP genes, respectively.

has_subtypes.name: Type 2B

has_subtypes.description: Autosomal recessive TFR2-related hemochromatosis, with earlier onset than HFE-related disease and iron accumulation in liver, heart, pancreas, and endocrine organs.

evidence.explanation: GeneReviews defines TFR2-related hemochromatosis as a biallelic TFR2 subtype.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of TFR2-HC is established in a proband with biallelic pathogenic variants in TFR2 identified by molecular genetic testing.

has_subtypes.name: Type 3

has_subtypes.description: Iron overload from heterozygous SLC40A1 variants, dominantly inherited unlike the HFE, HJV, HAMP and TFR2 types. The gene carries two distinct allelic classes. Gain-of-function variants make ferroportin resistant to hepcidin, so iron export continues unregulated and the picture is indistinguishable from the hepcidin-deficient types; this is the entity MONDO's definition of hemochromatosis type 4 describes, formerly called type 4B. Loss-of-function variants instead reduce ferroportin expression or its export capacity, retaining iron in macrophages, and give normal to low transferrin saturation with a tendency to anemia; that entity is ferroportin disease, formerly type 4A, which the same MONDO class carries as an exact synonym although the literature treats it as a separate condition.

evidence.explanation: Places SLC40A1 gain-of-function variants among the causes of haemochromatosis, the basis for this subtype row.
evidence.reference_title: Comparing the types of haemochromatosis- from genetics to clinics.
evidence.snippet: or a gain-of-function mutation in the gene encoding hepcidin receptor ferroportin (FPN1/SLC40A1)

evidence.explanation: Source for the two allelic classes of SLC40A1 described on this row and for the anaemia tendency of the loss-of-function class.

evidence.snippet: Also, gain-of-function ferroportin mutation is compared to ferroportin disease, which is a loss-of-function ferroportin mutation, and shows a tendency to anaemia.

has_subtypes.name: Type 4

has_subtypes.description: Dominantly inherited iron overload, reported in a Japanese family carrying an A49U point mutation in the iron-responsive element of ferritin H-subunit mRNA. The mutated element binds iron regulatory protein more tightly than wild type, so H-subunit translation stays repressed, and the authors attribute the tissue iron deposition to loss of the ferroxidase activity that the H subunit provides. ClinGen grades the FTH1 relationship to this disease Limited.

evidence.explanation: The report's own conclusion that the FTH1 IRE mutation causes hereditary iron overload through impaired H-subunit ferroxidase activity.
evidence.reference_title: A mutation, in the iron-responsive element of H ferritin mRNA, causing autosomal dominant iron overload.
evidence.snippet: These data suggest that the A49U mutation in the IRE of H-subunit is responsible for tissue iron deposition and is a novel cause of hereditary iron overload, most likely related to impairment of the ferroxidase activity generated by H subunit.

evidence.explanation: ClinGen records autosomal dominant inheritance and a Limited classification for FTH1 in hemochromatosis type 5.
evidence.snippet: FTH1 | HGNC:3976 | hemochromatosis type 5 | MONDO:0014225 | AD | Limited

evidence.explanation: The family reported segregates the iron overload dominantly.
evidence.reference_title: A mutation, in the iron-responsive element of H ferritin mRNA, causing autosomal dominant iron overload.
evidence.snippet: in four of seven members of a Japanese family affected by dominantly inherited iron overload
